items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: In my day The Meyer Davis it was Lester Lanin sort of stuff.

ctx.x: This is what got you gigs.

Yeah, yeah, but we didn't have that much, that many gigs, we didn't have that many gigs. Now, it's a corporate thing you know; it was a big deal, you know. In my day The Meyer Davis it was Lester Lanin sort of stuff. Now, all you have to do is play the melody. Anybody that has learned his instrument can play the melody and so the deviation became what is known as jazz, from the melody. Symphony players couldn't deviate. They were too disciplined to play what they had practiced all their lives.
